LESSON: READING 6.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Technology Suggested vocabulary Computer, record, type, information, internet, e
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Fluency, part of Technology Suggested vocabulary Computer, record, type, information, internet, e in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read well?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is heightened as they record what they have read in a personal journal.

• Communication and collaboration: Teamwork is developed as the learner participates actively in timed reading with peers, observing the rules of

engagement.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates the effort of others as they engage in timed reading and give positive feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is boosted as they read texts fluently.

46

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the reading fluency skills acquired when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
